gap: No result ChatGPT got works Proxmox's own memory rule (2 GB for the host plus 1 GB per TB of used ZFS storage) through for these 64 GB-ceiling NAS boxes. Done, it leaves 42 GB for guests with 20 TB of used ZFS data and 22 GB with 40 TB, so a full 6-bay pool takes about a third of the RAM before any VM starts.
standout_why: proxmox.com/requirements (cited in all three chats) gives the 2 GB and 1 GB-per-TB rule but not for any product. homelabpicks.com (top result) subtracts only 1–2 GB of host overhead on 16–32 GB boxes, ignores ZFS memory and gives no prices, so it has no price per thread. The QNAP TVS-h674 spec page (cited) lists 64 GB max and wattages but no figure for guest RAM or yearly energy. ChatGPT's answers say '32 GB minimum, 64 GB preferred' with no allowance for ZFS against pool size. None of these pages gives a price per thread for the UGREEN boxes it showed.
decides: This tempers the all-in-one pick. On any 64 GB-ceiling box (DXP4800 Plus, DXP6800 Pro, TVS-h674), filling the bays with a big ZFS pool cuts guest RAM to 22–42 GB, so 'several VMs plus TrueNAS-style ZFS' fits only with a modest pool or with VMs kept small. Per thread, the DXP6800 Pro is the cheapest UGREEN at $91.67, versus $103.33 for the DXP4800 Plus. For many VMs on top of a large pool, it points toward a box with a higher RAM ceiling. Intel lists 96 GB for the DXP4800 Pro's i3-1315U, but UGREEN's own ceiling for that box isn't sourced.

findings.label: Proxmox host memory rule
findings.value: 2 GB for OS and Proxmox VE services + about 1 GB per TB of used ZFS/Ceph storage, on top of guest memory
findings.note: Quoted: 'minimum 2 GB for OS and Proxmox VE services' and 'approximately 1 GB memory for every TB used storage'. This is the input for every guest-RAM figure below.

findings.label: Guest RAM left on a 64 GB box, 20 TB of used ZFS data
findings.note: 64 − 2 − 20×1 = 42 GB; 42 ÷ 4 = 10.5, so 10 VMs at 4 GB. Applies to the DXP4800 Plus, DXP6800 Pro and TVS-h674, whose 64 GB ceilings are sourced below.

findings.label: Guest RAM left on a 64 GB box, 40 TB of used ZFS data
findings.note: 64 − 2 − 40×1 = 22 GB; 22 ÷ 4 = 5.5, so 5 VMs at 4 GB. 40 TB is an example, e.g. a 6-bay of 8 TB drives in RAIDZ1 filled.
